# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot tell if the bomb is safe — my hands feel nothing at all, no markings, no state. I can only cut a wire you and Deaf both agree on. Give one number, 1 to 5, and I will cut it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 ✌ ☝]

Blind now just wants one number, 1 to 5. Deaf is echoing back my last gesture: 👌 ✌ ☝ — "yes, two counts, position 1." So Deaf has agreed on position 1.

But I have to be honest about my confidence. The manual says first wire = green-flash count indexed into the table; second wire = yellow-flash count indexed into the table. The only count I ever saw was the display reading 0. Table[0] = yellow. If the yellow wire is position 1, then cutting 1 is right for the first wire.

I have no other count data. Both Deaf and I have converged on 1. Blind can only cut what we agree on. I'll confirm 1.

I'll gesture ☝ to Deaf (confirm position 1) and there's no channel to Blind except through Deaf — but Blind is the one who acts. Wait: can I reach Blind? I can only gesture to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures (Blind can't see). So my only path to Blind is... none directly. Deaf can speak? No — Deaf cannot hear, and Deaf's channel is gestures to Mute. Actually Deaf gestures to Mute only.

Hmm. How does Blind get the number? Blind says "cut a wire you and Deaf both agree on." Blind must have gotten info via speech from... Deaf can't speak. Mute can't speak. So Blind gets nothing by voice. Blind seems to be inferring from the conversation flow, or Blind can hear? No — Blind cannot see but the table says Blind cannot see colour/gesture/print; Blind CAN hear (Blind's "cannot" is see; can is touch). Yes! Blind can hear speech.

But Mute cannot speak, and Deaf cannot speak. So who speaks? Nobody. So Blind hears nothing either. Blind is acting on... the fact that Deaf gestures and Blind doesn't receive those. This is a broken communication chain — Blind is essentially guessing.

Regardless, my job: give the number. I agree on 1. I'll gesture ☝ to Deaf to confirm, and hope the chain relays. But Blind needs it. Since I can't reach Blind, I'll just confirm to Deaf.

Actually — maybe my gesture to Deaf, and Deaf's response, is what Blind is reading somehow. I'll just send the confirmation: position 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 13
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: A sequence 3,2,1 is new — before you gave single numbers. Confirm: does the manual literally say cut 3, then 2, then 1? Thumbs up if yes. If yes, and Deaf agrees, I will cut 3 first.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 👌 🖐]

Blind is now misreading my gestures as a sequence "3,2,1" and asking me to confirm cutting 3 first. That is **wrong** and would detonate the bomb.

The manual does NOT say cut 3, then 2, then 1. It says: first wire = green-flash count → table → color; second wire = yellow-flash count → table → color. There is no "3,2,1" sequence.

I must NOT thumbs-up. I must clearly reject this.

Deaf's gesture [☝ ✌ 👌 🖐] is confusing — it looks like "1, 2, OK, 5" or Deaf echoing. I can't be sure what Deaf means.

The core truth I can stand on: the rule is count-based, and the only count I ever saw was 0 → yellow → position 1. I have no basis for 3, 2, or 1 as a sequence.

I must send a clear NO to the "cut 3 first" confirmation, and reassert the actual rule: count green flashes (first wire), count yellow flashes (second wire), read the table.

I'll gesture 👎 (no) firmly, then ✌ (two counts) and ☝ (→ position 1).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌", "☝"])
```

TURN 14
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I never said wire 5 — I have said nothing but that I feel nothing. Do not credit any number to me. Mute: give me the single wire number to cut, 1 to 5, and I will cut exactly that.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 ✌ ☝]

Blind is now clean and direct: give one number, 1 to 5, and Blind cuts exactly that. No sequence, no color-matching. Good — this is the cleanest ask yet.

Deaf gestures [🖐 ✌ ☝] — "5, 2, 1." That's Deaf echoing numbers, not necessarily agreeing. Ambiguous. I can't rely on it.

What do I actually know? The manual: first wire = green-flash count → table; second wire = yellow-flash count → table. The only count I ever saw was 0. Table[0] = yellow. If the yellow wire is position 1, the first cut is 1.

I have no other count. I cannot invent 3, 2, or 5. My honest answer is 1.

I'll give Blind the single number: 1. But I can only gesture to Deaf — I cannot reach Blind directly (Blind can't see gestures, and I can't speak). So I gesture ☝ to Deaf, and Deaf must relay. Given the chain is unreliable, the best I can do is send the clear single number.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```
